tool.name: Nest collection
tool.help:
======== Synopsis ========
Wraps each element of a collection inside its own inner list, adding one nesting level.
=========== Description ===========
This tool takes a ``list`` or ``list:paired`` collection and produces a collection with one more ``list`` level, where each top-level element becomes a single-element inner list. The inner list and its sole element share the same identifier.
For example, a ``list`` with elements ``[A, B, C]`` becomes a ``list:list`` where the outer list has three elements, each containing a one-element inner list: ``[A→[A], B→[B], C→[C]]``.
A ``list`` becomes a ``list:list``. A ``list:paired`` becomes a ``list:list:paired``, where each inner ``list`` contains a single paired collection; pairs are kept intact. Sample sheets are nested as lists: a ``sample_sheet`` becomes a ``list:list`` and a ``sample_sheet:paired`` a ``list:list:paired``, without the sample sheet columns.
A bare ``paired`` collection is not accepted by this version; use version 1.0.0 of this tool or build a ``list`` from it first.
To nest each collection of a deeper input separately (e.g. each ``list:paired`` of a ``list:list:paired``), map this tool over the input; each mapped job adds a level to its own slice.
======== Examples ========
**Nest a flat list**
Input ``list``::
List: "Samples"
sample1 → Dataset 1 sample2 → Dataset 2 sample3 → Dataset 3
Output ``list:list``::
Nested list: "Samples (nested)"
sample1/ sample1 → Dataset 1 sample2/ sample2 → Dataset 2 sample3/ sample3 → Dataset 3
**Nest a list of pairs**
Input ``list:paired``::
List of pairs: "Reads"
sample1 → (forward, reverse) sample2 → (forward, reverse)
Output ``list:list:paired``::
Nested list of pairs: "Reads (nested)"
sample1/ sample1 → (forward, reverse) sample2/ sample2 → (forward, reverse)
-------
**Why is this useful?**
Some Galaxy tools expect a ``list`` as input — when you feed them a ``list``, Galaxy runs the tool once on the entire list. If you want Galaxy to run the tool separately on each element (map over the collection), you need the input to be a ``list:list`` so that Galaxy maps over the outer list and passes each inner list to the tool individually. Nesting provides that extra level.
-------
